summary: Firefinder on a second-floor window of the 1907 St. Johns City Hall, Portland, from 1952. The building was still standing at 2021 visits; sources say abandoned, not gone.

facts.design: Firefinder mounted on an exterior brick wall, viewed from a second-floor window of the St. Johns City Hall building
facts.status_note: The building still stood at 2021 visits. The firefinder lookout is described as abandoned; no source we read says whether the firefinder remains on the wall.

access.note: A 2021 visitor says the building cannot be entered without an appointment.

events.note: Building constructed as the city hall for St. Johns City
Engine Company 32 stationed in the historic city hall, per Portland's Station 22 history
Building converted to a fire station (one source's date; see resolved_conflicts)
August 1951 fire burned 2,400 acres, about 25 percent of Forest Park; led to emergency lookouts
Portland Parks Bureau, with Engine 32, mounted a firefinder on the exterior wall at a second-floor window
Engine Company 32 moved out of the city hall when its new station was built
Survey crew found the original cupola and flagpole already removed from the building

corrections.why: Two 2021 visits describe the building as still standing, and firelookout.com says the lookout is still there. The FFLA Oregon list says Abandoned, not gone. No source says the building was demolished. The lookout use ended; the building did not.

The 1952 set-up was a firefinder on an exterior wall at a second-floor window, with no lookout cab. The vocabulary's point (firefinder only) fits better than rooftop. Editor to confirm, since a cupola now sits on the roof.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Roaming Civic and WillhiteWeb give 1915. Portland's Station 22 history says Engine Company 32 was in the city hall from 1913. The story reports both and does not choose.
The Roaming Civic says city Park Rangers; WillhiteWeb says Portland Police. Both are 2021 visits. The story reports both.

The brief record says gone. Firelookout.com says Abandoned. Still there; the FFLA list says Abandoned; both 2021 visits say the building stands. The story follows the 2021 visits and the correction above proposes standing.

sources.title: St. Johns Lookout Site, Portland Oregon

notes_for_editor: The brief record's status gone is contradicted by two 2021 visits (Roaming Civic, WillhiteWeb) and by firelookout.com's still there; the FFLA list says Abandoned. The proposed status is standing and kind point; both need editor sign-off. Unresolved: whether the firefinder is still mounted (no source says); the cupola's date (WillhiteWeb suspects 1964 or 1996 rebuild); the occupant (Park Rangers or Police). Not read: a search snippet from portlandfirehistory.com says Engine 32 served the station until September 8, 1959, which conflicts with Station 22's 1954 date; check before using it. Also not read: a 2010 Flickr page on the same cupola (search snippet). The WillhiteWeb 2021 photos have no captured URLs, so none are added to photos. Access comes only from one 2021 blog visit; check before saying more. Agency in the record is Portland City Parks (firelookout.com); facts use Portland Parks Bureau (Forest Lookouts). Same body, different names.
